runtime_row.questionText: A student carries out an experiment and plots the V–I graph of three samples of nichrome wire with resistances R₁, R₂ and R₃ respectively (Figure 12.5). Which of the following is true?
solutionSteps: [1 mark] In Figure 12.5 the current I is on the y-axis and V on the x-axis, so the slope of each line is I/V = 1/R: the LESS steep the line, the HIGHER the resistance. The line for R₁ is steepest and R₃ is least steep, with R₂ in between, so R₃ > R₂ > R₁. Correct option (c).

runtime_row.questionText: Three 2 Ω resistors, A, B and C, are connected as shown in Figure 12.7. Each of them dissipates energy and can withstand a maximum power of 18 W without melting. Find the maximum current that can flow through the three resistors?
runtime_row.answer: From the figure, A is in series with the parallel combination of B and C. For each resistor: P = I²R ⇒ maximum permissible current in any single 2 Ω resistor = √(P_max/R) = √(18/2) = √9 = 3 A. Resistor A carries the full circuit current I, so its limit is I ≤ 3 A. Resistors B and C share the current equally (identical), so each carries I/2; their limit allows I ≤ 2 × 3 = 6 A. The binding constraint is A. Therefore the maximum current that can flow through the main circuit (through A) is 3 A; through each of B and C the current is 1.5 A.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] From P = I²R, the maximum current any single 2 Ω resistor can carry is I_max(one) = √(P/R) = √(18/2) = √9 = 3 A.
[0.5 mark] Per the figure, A is in series with the parallel combination of B and C, so the current I through A is the total circuit current.
[0.5 mark] Identical B and C each carry I/2.
[0.5 mark] Limit from A: I ≤ 3 A. Limit from B (or C): I/2 ≤ 3 A ⇒ I ≤ 6 A. The tighter limit is from A.
[0.5 mark] Hence maximum total current through the circuit is 3 A (with 1.5 A through each of B and C).
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Maximum total current = 3 A (1.5 A each through B and C).

runtime_row.questionText: In the circuit diagram given in Fig. 11.10, suppose the resistors R₁, R₂ and R₃ have the values 5 Ω, 10 Ω, 30 Ω, respectively, which have been connected to a battery of 12 V. Calculate (a) the current through each resistor, (b) the total current in the circuit, and (c) the total circuit resistance.
runtime_row.answer: Three resistors are in parallel with a 12 V battery, so each has 12 V across it. (a) I₁ = 12/5 = 2.4 A; I₂ = 12/10 = 1.2 A; I₃ = 12/30 = 0.4 A. (b) I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃ = 2.4 + 1.2 + 0.4 = 4 A. (c) 1/R_p = 1/5 + 1/10 + 1/30 = 6/30 + 3/30 + 1/30 = 10/30 = 1/3 ⇒ R_p = 3 Ω.
solutionSteps: [0.5 mark] In parallel each resistor has the full battery voltage V = 12 V across it.
[1 mark] (b) Total current I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃ = 2.4 + 1.2 + 0.4 = 4 A.
[0.5 mark] Cross-check: I = V/R_p = 12/3 = 4 A. Consistent.

runtime_row.questionText: If in Fig. 11.12, R₁ = 10 Ω, R₂ = 40 Ω, R₃ = 30 Ω, R₄ = 20 Ω, R₅ = 60 Ω, and a 12 V battery is connected to the arrangement. Calculate (a) the total resistance in the circuit, and (b) the total current flowing in the circuit.
runtime_row.answer: R₁ and R₂ are in parallel: 1/R' = 1/10 + 1/40 = 5/40 ⇒ R' = 8 Ω. R₃, R₄ and R₅ are in parallel: 1/R'' = 1/30 + 1/20 + 1/60 = 2/60 + 3/60 + 1/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 ⇒ R'' = 10 Ω. The two combinations are then in series: R = R' + R'' = 8 + 10 = 18 Ω. (a) Total resistance = 18 Ω. (b) Total current I = V/R = 12/18 = 0.67 A.
solutionSteps: [0.5 mark] These two equivalent resistors R' and R'' are in series.
[1 mark] Total resistance: R = R' + R'' = 8 + 10 = 18 Ω.
[1 mark] Total current: I = V/R = 12 / 18 = 2/3 ≈ 0.67 A.

runtime_row.questionText: (A) V-I graph for a nichrome wire is shown in the diagram. (i) Prove that the graph follows Ohm's law and calculate the resistance of nichrome wire from the given V-I graph. (ii) (I) Calculate the equivalent resistance of the combination of resistors connected in the given circuit. (II) Find the value of the total current drawn from the battery. OR (B) (i) Define the SI unit of power. Express the electric power of an electric appliance in terms of potential difference and current flowing through it. (ii) In a house, 3 bulbs of 100 W each, are lit for 5 hours daily and an electric heater of 1.0 kW is used for half an hour daily. Calculate the total energy consumed in a month of 30 days and its cost at the rate of ₹ 3.60 per kWh. (iii) Convert the commercial unit of electric energy into Joule (J).
runtime_row.answer: (A) (i) Straight line through the origin ⇒ Ohm's law; R = slope = 4 Ω. (ii) (I) Equivalent resistance = 15 Ω; (II) I = 5/15 = 1/3 A. OR (B) (i) 1 W = 1 J/s; P = VI. (ii) Total energy in 30 days = 60 kWh; cost = ₹216. (iii) 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (A) (i) The V–I graph is a straight line passing through the origin (V ∝ I), so it follows Ohm's law. R = slope of the V–I graph = (0.8 − 0.4)/(0.2 − 0.1) = 0.4/0.1 = 4 Ω (any other two points on the line give the same value).

[1 mark] (ii) (I) The 3 Ω and 7 Ω resistors are in series: Rₛ = 3 + 7 = 10 Ω. Rₛ is in parallel with the 10 Ω resistor: 1/Rₚ = 1/10 + 1/10 ⇒ Rₚ = 5 Ω. The other two 5 Ω resistors are in series with Rₚ.
[1 mark] Net resistance R = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 Ω. (II) Total current drawn from the 5 V battery I = V/R = 5/15 = 1/3 A ≈ 0.33 A.

[1 mark] OR (B) (i) The SI unit of power is the watt: the power of a device that consumes 1 joule of energy in 1 second (1 W = 1 J/s), or that carries 1 A at a potential difference of 1 V (1 W = 1 V × 1 A). Electric power P = VI.

[1 mark] (ii) E = P × t. Energy of the 3 bulbs = 3 × 100 W × 5 h = 1500 Wh = 1.5 kWh; energy of the heater = 1.0 kW × 0.5 h = 0.5 kWh; total per day = 2 kWh; total for 30 days = 30 × 2 = 60 kWh; cost = 60 × ₹3.60 = ₹216. (iii) 1 kWh = 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (A) (i) Straight line through the origin ⇒ Ohm's law; R = slope = 4 Ω. (ii) (I) Equivalent resistance = 15 Ω; (II) I = 5/15 = 1/3 A. OR (B) (i) 1 W = 1 J/s; P = VI. (ii) Total energy in 30 days = 60 kWh; cost = ₹216. (iii) 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

fields.answer: (i) The SI unit of power is the watt: 1 W is the power of a device that consumes 1 J of energy in 1 s (1 W = 1 J/s), i.e. that carries 1 A at a potential difference of 1 V. P = VI. (ii) Energy per day = 1.5 kWh + 0.5 kWh = 2 kWh; in 30 days = 60 kWh; cost = 60 × ₹3.60 = ₹216. (iii) 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

runtime_row.subject: Science
runtime_row.questionText: (A) (i) Derive an expression for the equivalent resistance of three resistors connected in parallel with a battery as shown in figure. (ii) Find the values of the electric currents flowing through the resistors R1, R2 and R3 in the given electric circuit. OR (B) (i) Define electrical resistivity of a material. (ii) How will the resistivity and resistance of a conducting wire change if the length and area of cross-section of wire both are doubled ? Justify your answer. (iii) Calculate the electric current flowing through a 4 Ω resistor that produces 100 J of heat every second.
runtime_row.answer: (A) (i) 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃. (ii) I₁ = 12/2 = 6 A, I₂ = 12/4 = 3 A, I₃ = 12/6 = 2 A. OR (B) (i) Resistivity = resistance of a wire of unit length and unit area of cross-section. (ii) Resistivity unchanged (property of the material); resistance unchanged since l/A is unchanged. (iii) H = I²Rt ⇒ I = √(100/4) = 5 A.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] (A) (i) In a parallel combination the potential difference V across each resistor is the same.
[0.5 mark] Current through each resistor: I₁ = V/R₁,
[0.5 mark] I₂ = V/R₂, I₃ = V/R₃.

[1 mark] If Rₚ is the resistance of the parallel combination, the current drawn from the battery is I = V/Rₚ, and I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃ ⇒ V/Rₚ = V/R₁ + V/R₂ + V/R₃ ⇒ 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃. (ii) All three resistors are in parallel across the 12 V battery: I₁ = 12/2 = 6 A, I₂ = 12/4 = 3 A, I₃ = 12/6 = 2 A. OR (B) (i) Resistivity is the resistance offered by a wire of the material of unit length and unit area of cross-section (ρ = RA/l; SI unit Ω m).

[1 mark] (ii) Resistivity remains the same — it is a characteristic property of the material, independent of its dimensions. Resistance R = ρl/A also remains the same, because doubling both l and A leaves l/A unchanged.
[1 mark] (iii) H = I²Rt ⇒ 100 J = I² × 4 Ω × 1 s ⇒ I² = 25 ⇒ I = 5 A.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: (A) (i) 1/Rₚ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + 1/R₃. (ii) I₁ = 12/2 = 6 A, I₂ = 12/4 = 3 A, I₃ = 12/6 = 2 A. OR (B) (i) Resistivity = resistance of a wire of unit length and unit area of cross-section. (ii) Resistivity unchanged (property of the material); resistance unchanged since l/A is unchanged. (iii) H = I²Rt ⇒ I = √(100/4) = 5 A.

runtime_row.questionText: Fig. 1 shows the filament in a lamp. The filament is made from a very thin piece of metal. When there is a current in the filament it glows brightly and becomes very hot. Explain how the current causes the filament to become hot.
runtime_row.answer: The filament metal has resistance; work is done against the resistance by the moving electrons; this releases heat energy; electrical energy is transferred to thermal/heat energy.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] The filament metal has resistance which opposes the flow of charge.
[1 mark] Work is done against this resistance by the electrons as they move through the wire.
[1 mark] As the electrons collide with the ions of the metal lattice, heat energy is released.
[1 mark] Electrical energy is thereby transferred to thermal (heat) energy, so the filament becomes very hot and glows.
runtime_row.finalAnswer: Electrical energy is converted to heat energy because work is done by the moving electrons against the filament's resistance, raising its temperature.
